claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution; the components inside it inherit the package's version.
A source-based plugin package's version is the Git tag on its repository.
Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow: apply a semver Git tag, then run `pulumi package publish`.
`pulumi package publish` sends package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.
Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry.
Source-based packages referenced directly from a Pulumi.yaml file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), even if not a valid semantic version.
Executable-based plugin packages are distributed as pre-built plugin binaries, typically with per-language SDKs published to feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
An executable-based package's version is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can publish executable-based packages to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
Pulumi recommends that a repository contain exactly one Pulumi package, regardless of package type.
Multiple components inside a single package are fine and ship together at the package's version.
The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with supporting components to secure and operate it.
One PulumiPlugin.yaml at the repository root defines the package, with components living alongside it.
Pulumi does not recommend a single monorepo containing one giant package for all of an organization's components.
When unrelated components share a package, every release versions every component the same way, which violates semver.
